title: Catalog
description: Every list of kinds in the game. Kinds are data: code reads their properties, never their names.

sailors.description: The figures that sail the boats. The first is the one drawn until players choose their own.

regimes.description: The kinds of spell of weather.

WeatherSea.title: WeatherSea
WeatherSea.description: The waves long enough to move a boat: the band of wavelengths they span and the spectrum that gives each its height.

sigmaBelow.description: The peak's width below the peak frequency.

sigmaAbove.description: The peak's width above the peak frequency.

spreading.description: The directional spreading's exponent s in cos²ˢ(θ/2): a whole number.

fetchCap.description: The fetch of open water, in nautical miles.

cull.description: Waves lower than this fraction of an area's highest are left out.

breaking.description: The most significant height the waves keep in shallow water, as a share of its depth: where the water is shallower than the sea's height over this, its waves are capped to it and break.

swellLeast.description: A swell lower than this, in m, is none.

swellSpreading.description: The swell's directional spreading's exponent s in cos²ˢ(θ/2) about the way it travels: a whole number.

swellSigma.description: The swell's spectrum's width: a Gaussian in frequency, its standard deviation as a share of its peak frequency.

swellSteps.description: Newton's steps that find when the swell arriving at a place left its system: a whole number.

currentMost.description: The most a current against them raises the waves, as a multiple of their height in still water; a wave the current blocks is raised this much.

shadowLeast.description: The least share of a swell that reaches behind land.

leeReach.description: How far upwind of a place land calms its waves, in m: the shelter's tables hold the lee's fetch in steps of 4 m, at most 254 of them.

WeatherDisk.title: WeatherDisk
WeatherDisk.description: The wind over the disk: how its speed rises toward the rim, the refuge at the centre, the stronger gusts of the outer waters and the turning of the difference across the disk.

speedCentre.description: The wind's speed at the centre, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

speedRim.description: The wind's speed at the rim, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

rim.description: Where the speed reaches its share at the rim: the mist band, in nautical miles.

refugeInner.description: Within this the refuge's limits hold in full, in nautical miles.

refugeOuter.description: Beyond this the refuge's limits do not hold, in nautical miles.

refugeMeanKnee.description: The refuge softens the mean wind above this, in knots.

refugeMean.description: The mean wind the refuge holds to, in knots.

refugeWindKnee.description: The refuge softens the wind with its gusts above this, in knots.

refugeWind.description: The wind with its gusts the refuge holds to, in knots.

refugeSwellKnee.description: The refuge softens the storms' swell above this, in m.

refugeSwell.description: The swell the refuge holds to, in m: above its knee.

rimGusts.description: The gust factor's excess over 1 grows by this share toward the rim.

rimGustsFrom.description: From here to the rim, in nautical miles.

acrossTurn.description: The shortest and longest time the axis of the wind's difference across the disk takes to turn once, in hours.

edge.description: The lip of the falls: the disk's radius, in nautical miles.

fallDraftFrom.description: The falls draw the air toward the lip from here, in nautical miles.

fallDraft.description: How fast the falls draw the air at the lip, in knots.

WeatherCurrent.title: WeatherCurrent
WeatherCurrent.description: The water's own motion: the circulation round the disk and the drain toward the falls, each linear between its points, nothing before the first and its last value beyond the last, falling off in shallow water.

circulationAt.description: The circulation's points, from the centre, in nautical miles.

circulation.description: Its speed at each point, in knots.

drainAt.description: The drain's points, from the centre, in nautical miles: the last is the lip.

drain.description: Its speed toward the lip at each point, in knots.

shallow.description: In water shallower than this the current falls off in proportion to the depth, in m.

WeatherGusts.title: WeatherGusts
WeatherGusts.description: The gust field: gradient noise in three octaves, each with cells and a life half its predecessor's, carried downwind.

gustAlong.description: The largest cells along the wind, in m.

gustAcross.description: The largest cells across the wind, in m.

gustLife.description: The largest cells' life, in s.

gustSpeed.description: How fast the field travels, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

gustVeer.description: How far the strongest gust veers, and the deepest lull backs by half, in degrees.

change.description: How long one spell takes to give way to the next, in minutes.

WeatherRing.title: WeatherRing
WeatherRing.description: The beginners' ring round gusts heading for the boat.

threshold.description: A patch gets a ring when its gust factor is this far from 1 toward the spell's.

spacing.description: The grid the field is sampled on upwind of the boat, in m.

depth.description: How far upwind the grid reaches, in m.

width.description: How wide the grid is across the wind, in m.

reach.description: A patch's track must pass this close to the boat, in m.

rate.description: Samplings of the field a second.

WeatherWaveWind.title: WeatherWaveWind
WeatherWaveWind.description: The wind that raises the waves: an exponential average of the mean wind at each sea area's centre.

waveTimeConstant.description: The average's time constant, in s.

waveSample.description: The wind is sampled on a grid of world time this far apart, in s: a whole number of seconds.

Regime.title: Regime
Regime.description: A kind of spell of weather.

share.description: The regime's share of the world's time.

frontal.description: A spell of it arrives and leaves as a front does: a front crosses the disk, and the wind veers.

spell.description: The shortest and the longest a spell of it lasts, in hours.

pressure.description: The lowest and the highest of its pressure's level, in hPa.

next.description: The regimes a spell of it gives way to, with the chance of each.

systems.description: The systems born in a spell of it.

cumulus.description: How much of the sky its fair-weather cumulus covers, from 0 to 1.

RegimeWind.title: RegimeWind
RegimeWind.description: A regime's wind, from which each spell's is drawn.

speed.description: The least and the most of its wind at mid-disk, in knots.

gustFactor.description: Its strongest gusts as a multiple of the mean wind.

shift.description: How far its two oscillating shifts swing together, in degrees each way.

period.description: The shortest and the longest period of a shift, in minutes.

across.description: How far the wind's direction differs from the centre to the rim, in degrees.

drift.description: The most its direction moves over a spell, in degrees.

RegimeNext.title: RegimeNext
RegimeNext.description: A regime a spell may give way to.

chance.description: The chance a spell gives way to it.

RegimeSystems.title: RegimeSystems
RegimeSystems.description: How many systems of a kind are born in a spell.

rate.description: How many are born an hour over the disk, on average.

atStart.description: How many are born as the spell begins.

peak.description: Their peak wind is drawn from between these shares of their kind's range: [0, 0.5] for the lower half.

when.description: When they are born: at any time, by day only, or at night only.

WeatherFront.title: WeatherFront
WeatherFront.description: A front: a line across the disk lying in a trough, the old spell ahead of it and the new behind.

troughAhead.description: The trough deepens toward the line as e^(−s / this), in nautical miles.

troughBehind.description: And fills behind it within this, a Gaussian's width, in nautical miles.

frontWind.description: Its own wind at its steepest, in knots.

frontTurning.description: Its wind blows toward the trough turned clockwise by this, in degrees.

blend.description: The spells blend across the line within this either side, in nautical miles.

frontGusts.description: The gust factor's excess rises by this behind the line.

gustsBehind.description: Over this behind the line, in nautical miles.

WeatherPressure.title: WeatherPressure
WeatherPressure.description: The pressure: its slope across the disk, and its rise behind a front.

slope.description: The slope across the disk, low on the left of the base wind, in hPa a knot of it a nautical mile.

rise.description: How fast the pressure rises behind a front's line, in hPa a minute.

ease.description: At a change of spell with no front, the level moves from the old spell's to the new over this from the change's start, in minutes.

WeatherReach.title: WeatherReach
WeatherReach.description: How far the systems reach: their weakening toward the centre, and where they end.

inwardFrom.description: Within this of the centre a system is at its weakest, in nautical miles.

inwardTo.description: Beyond this it is whole, in nautical miles.

inwardLeast.description: What a front, a squall or a shower keeps of itself at its weakest.

cut.description: A system reaches this many of its widths from its centre.

SystemSwell.title: SystemSwell
SystemSwell.description: The swell a kind of system raises, by its strength: a long, low lift that runs ahead of it at its group speed, its longest waves first.

period.description: The least and the most of a system's swell's peak period, drawn per system, in s.

band.description: The shortest and the longest period its swell spans, in s.

height.description: Its significant height at the system's edge at full strength, in m: the first at the least of the kind's wind, the second at the most.

SystemCloud.title: SystemCloud
SystemCloud.description: The cloud of a kind of system: its form, its heights and reach at its whole, and how far its cloud grows ahead of its wind.

base.description: Its base above the sea, in m.

top.description: Its top at its whole, in m.

reach.description: How far its top reaches from its centre at its whole, behind and ahead along its track, as shares of its size.

deck.description: Its deck of low cloud about the centre at its whole: its reach as a share of its size, and its top in m; no reach for none.

lead.description: Its cloud strength is its strength times this, at most 1: at 2 its cloud is whole when its wind is half grown.

dark.description: How dark its base is, from 0 to 1.

CloudForm.title: CloudForm
CloudForm.description: A cloud's form, which names how it is drawn: fair cumulus, a towering cumulonimbus with its anvil and shelf, a storm's deck with its towers, fog, or none.

SystemSheets.title: SystemSheets
SystemSheets.description: The sheet cloud about a system's centre, by its cloud strength: for each layer where it begins and where it is whole, as shares of its size.

cirrus.description: Its outflow cirrus: from, and whole within.

middle.description: The middle sheet: from, and whole within.

low.description: Low overcast: from, and whole within.

SystemRain.title: SystemRain
SystemRain.description: The rain under a kind of system, at its full strength.

rate.description: Its rate at its core, in mm an hour; 0 for none.

width.description: A core's width, or the bands' reach, as a share of its size.

bands.description: Its rain falls in this many spiral bands about its centre; 0 for a core.

turn.description: The bands turn once in this many minutes; 0 for never.

SystemKind.title: SystemKind
SystemKind.description: A kind of weather system: a pressure shape moving with it, its wind turned from the pressure's gradient, its size, life and track.

name.description: What the chart, the forecast and the key call it.

key.description: Its line in the chart's key.

symbol.description: How the chart draws it: a squall's dark cell, a shower's heap, a storm's spiral, a low's spiral lettered L, a fog bank, a patch of calm, a squall line's dash, dot, dot, a trough's dashes.

shape.description: A dome, a line (a dome stretched across its motion along its length), a low, or none: a patch that scales the wind.

turning.description: Its wind blows toward lower pressure turned clockwise by this, in degrees.

width.description: Its pressure's or its patch's Gaussian width, as a share of its size.

ahead.description: A dome is steeper ahead: its distance along its track is times this ahead of its centre.

broad.description: A low's broad low about its core: its share of the depth, and its width as a multiple of the core's.

stretch.description: A patch is stretched along its track by this.

inward.description: How it weakens toward the centre: weak to the least, gone to nothing, or none.

gusts.description: The gust factor's excess rises by this near its core.

size.description: Its radius, the least and the most, in nautical miles: a line's half its depth along its motion.

length.description: A line's length across its motion, the least and the most, in nautical miles; nothing for any other shape.

speed.description: How fast it moves, the least and the most: a share of the base wind, or knots.

speedOf.description: Whether speed is a share of the base wind or knots.

life.description: How long it lives, the least and the most, in minutes.

wind.description: The wind it adds at its peak at full strength, the least and the most, in knots.

factor.description: A patch's share of the wind at its core, the least and the most.

depth.description: Its pressure at its centre at full strength, the least and the most, in hPa: a dome's above, a low's below.

track.description: Where it is born and how it moves: wind, across from the windward rim; outer, round the outer waters; drift, inside, drifting with the wind.

turnsIn.description: Of those that keep to the outer waters, the share that turn inward, closing on the centre.

islands.description: The share of those born by day that are born over an island's land.

night.description: It is born only at night, or within dawn minutes after sunrise.

dawn.description: Minutes after sunrise it may still be born.

lift.description: It lifts this long after sunrise, the least and the most, in minutes.

calmBelow.description: It is born only where the spell's mean wind is under this, in knots; 0 for anywhere.

goneAbove.description: It is gone once the spell's mean wind passes this, in knots; 0 for never.

SystemLightning.title: SystemLightning
SystemLightning.description: The lightning from a kind of system: above a strength, at a rate rising with it, struck within a ring about its centre.

above.description: It flashes at or above this strength.

rate.description: Its flashes a minute at full strength, rising from none at above.

within.description: Its flashes strike between these shares of its size from its centre.

SystemFog.title: SystemFog
SystemFog.description: The fog of a fog bank: its visibility at its core at the sea, drawn per bank, and how it thins with height.

core.description: Its visibility at its core at full strength, the least and the most, in m.

height.description: Its density falls as e^(−h / height) above the sea, in m.

WeatherVisibility.title: WeatherVisibility
WeatherVisibility.description: Visibility: the contrast a thing is seen at, and the words for it.

contrast.description: A thing is seen while the optical depth to it is at most this: ln of the contrast threshold's inverse.

words.description: Visibility is very poor under the first, poor under the second, moderate under the third and good above, in m.

WeatherLightning.title: WeatherLightning
WeatherLightning.description: Lightning: the slots of world time a flash is drawn in, its share to the sea and its strokes.

slot.description: World time is cut into slots this long, each holding a flash or none, in s: a whole number.

sea.description: The share of flashes that strike the sea; the rest stay in the cloud.

single.description: The share of flashes of a single stroke; the rest have from two to most, evenly.

most.description: The most strokes a flash has.

apart.description: The strokes' geometric mean interval, in ms.

WeatherThunder.title: WeatherThunder
WeatherThunder.description: Thunder: how far it is heard, how fast it comes, how long it rolls and where it cracks.

heard.description: It is heard within this of its flash, in nautical miles.

speed.description: The speed of sound, in m/s.

longest.description: It rolls at most this long, in s.

crack.description: Within this of its channel it begins with a crack, in m.

WeatherWeek.title: WeatherWeek
WeatherWeek.description: A world's week of weather: how it is drawn and checked.

opening.description: A world opens with this long of settled or trade weather and no front on the disk, in hours.

closing.description: And closes with this long of one spell of closingRegime and no front on the disk, in hours.

fair.description: Its longest settled or trade spell is at least this long, in hours.

shares.description: Each regime's share is within this of the catalog's.

sharesFrom.description: For a world of this many days or more.

margin.description: The week covers this long beyond the world's end, in hours.

draws.description: The most weeks drawn before the best is kept.

veer.description: How far the wind veers as a cold front passes, the least and the most, in degrees.

warmVeer.description: And as a warm front passes: a change from a regime of no front into a frontal one comes as a warm front, every other front as a cold one.

swing.description: How far the wind's direction may move either way at another change, in degrees.

frontSpeed.description: How fast a front moves, the least and the most, in knots.

frontTrough.description: How deep a front's trough is, the least and the most, in hPa.

spread.description: A front moves toward where the new spell's wind blows, within this either way, in degrees.

wobble.description: The most a system wobbles off its track, in nautical miles.

wobblePeriod.description: The shortest and the longest period of a wobble, in minutes.

strengthWobble.description: The most a system's strength wobbles, as a share of it.

systemsMost.description: The most systems on the disk at once.

fill.description: The kind born wherever the disk would otherwise be empty after the opening, so the chart always has weather on it.

outer.description: The outer waters the kinds that keep to them are born in, from and to, in nautical miles from the centre.

seed.description: The seed a developer's held spells are drawn with.

WeekMost.title: WeekMost
WeekMost.description: The most systems of a kind on the disk at once: one more is not born.

WeekQuiet.title: WeekQuiet
WeekQuiet.description: Kinds kept off the water in a world's first hours and in its closing spell, so the rush to discover and the closing race stay fair; and, in a spell of a regime of no front, no storm turns inward.

hours.description: None is born in the world's first this many hours.

WeekLineAhead.title: WeekLineAhead
WeekLineAhead.description: A line of a kind born ahead of every cold front into a regime, moving with the front.

ahead.description: How far ahead of the front's line, the least and the most, in nautical miles.

WeatherForecast.title: WeatherForecast
WeatherForecast.description: The forecast: how often it is issued, how far ahead it runs, its gale warnings and a place's outlook. It is the truth: every system and every front where it will be.

every.description: It is issued at each boundary of this many minutes of world time from the world's epoch.

horizon.description: It runs this far ahead, in minutes.

step.description: In steps of this many minutes: the horizon is a whole number of them, at most 12.

ForecastGale.title: ForecastGale
ForecastGale.description: A gale warning: where the synoptic wind of a step reaches a gale, on a grid over the water.

mean.description: A gale where the mean wind reaches this, in knots.

gust.description: Or the typical strongest gust reaches this, in knots.

quantile.description: The typical strongest gust is the gust field's value of this quantile: its 90th percentile.

grid.description: The grid's spacing, in nautical miles.

within.description: Over the water within this of the centre, in nautical miles.

ForecastOutlook.title: ForecastOutlook
ForecastOutlook.description: A place's outlook in the words of the shipping forecast: when it is sampled, what is a change and the times' words.

samples.description: It is sampled at these minutes from the issue, ascending.

turn.description: A change where the wind's direction turns this far or more, in degrees.

forces.description: Or its force changes by this many or more.

imminent.description: Imminent: within this of the issue, in minutes.

soon.description: Soon: within this, later beyond, in minutes.

WeatherKeyframe.title: WeatherKeyframe
WeatherKeyframe.description: The systems' keyframes, which the server and the phone interpolate between.

every.description: Seconds between keyframes: a whole number.

WeatherWater.title: WeatherWater
WeatherWater.description: The water's signs of the wind: the mean wind sampled round the camera, against the wave wind.

WeatherClouds.title: WeatherClouds
WeatherClouds.description: Clouds and rain: the sheets' layers and the lattice they are held on, the fair-weather cumulus, the islands' caps, a front's sheets and rain, and rain's words and visibility.

middle.description: The middle sheet's height, in m.

lattice.description: The sheets' cover is held at the corners of a world-fixed lattice this far apart, in m, and is bilinear between them.

cumulusCell.description: The fair-weather cumulus's lattice cells, in m.

cumulusJitter.description: Each cloud stands up to this share of a cell from its cell's centre.

cumulusTops.description: Their tops, the lowest and the highest, in m.

cumulusSize.description: Their radius, the least and the most, in m.

cumulusLife.description: Each cell holds a cloud for this long, growing over its first quarter and shrinking over its last, in minutes.

capSun.description: An island's cap grows as the sun at it rises from the first to the second height, and shrinks as it sinks, in degrees.

capTops.description: A cap's top, over the narrowest island and the widest, in m.

capWidth.description: A cap's radius, as a share of its island's width.

capStreet.description: How many cumulus trail downwind of a cap, a cell apart.

frontCirrus.description: A front's cirrus: where it begins ahead of the line and where it is whole, and where it begins to clear behind it and where it is gone, in nautical miles.

frontLow.description: Its low cloud: a band this far behind the line and this wide, in nautical miles.

frontRain.description: Its rain: the rate at the band's middle, in mm an hour, the band this far behind the line and this wide, in nautical miles.

frontWarm.description: A warm front's rain and low cloud, ahead of its line: the rate at the band's middle, in mm an hour, the band this far ahead of the line and this wide, in nautical miles.

rainWords.description: Rain is light under the first rate, moderate under the second, heavy under the third and violent above, in mm an hour.

rainExtinction.description: Rain's extinction, a R^b per km of rain of R mm an hour: a and b.

rainScale.description: Visibility on the game's stage is this share of the real.

Encounters.title: Encounters
Encounters.description: Boats meeting: their hulls touching, the wind one takes from another, and the Articles, the right-of-way rules that judge them.

EncountersContact.title: EncountersContact
EncountersContact.description: Two hulls touching: an impulse with no damage.

restitution.description: The share of the closing speed the hulls part with.

friction.description: Coulomb's coefficient of the hulls sliding along each other.

passes.description: Passes of the impulses over a tick's contacts.

push.description: The share of the rest of the penetration pushed apart in a tick.

cap.description: The most a contact pushes boats apart in a tick, in m.

apart.description: Ticks two boats must be apart before touching again is a new bump.

EncountersShadow.title: EncountersShadow
EncountersShadow.description: The wind shadow: the wake a sail leaves along its apparent wind, in units of its rig's height h above the water.

deficit.description: A: the share of the wind lost on the wake's axis one rig height behind.

near.description: s₀: closer than this, in h, the loss is no greater.

width.description: w: the wake's half-width parameter at one rig height, in h.

header.description: H: how far the wake turns the wind one rig height behind, in degrees.

deflection.description: How far the wake turns from the apparent wind toward the source's windward side: close-hauled, and on a reach and beyond, in degrees.

deflectionAt.description: The apparent wind angles at which each deflection holds, between which it blends, in degrees.

reach.description: How far the wake reaches, in h.

taper.description: Where it begins to fade to nothing at its reach, in h.

sources.description: The most wakes a boat feels at once: the nearest.

EncountersArticles.title: EncountersArticles
EncountersArticles.description: The numbers the Articles are computed with.

room.description: A boat that acquires right of way, or changes course, must give room for this long, in s.

turn.description: A change of course is one of more than this, in degrees.

course.description: The time constant of a boat's course: its heading, smoothed, in s.

pairs.description: Boats closer than this many hull lengths are remembered as a pair.

headToWind.description: Within this of head to wind a boat keeps the tack she had, in degrees.

EncountersOverlay.title: EncountersOverlay
EncountersOverlay.description: The beginners' right-of-way overlay, and dirty air drawn in the wind overlay.

range.description: Boats within this are considered, in m.

ahead.description: How far ahead their present motions are followed, in s.

close.description: A boat is marked when it comes within this many hull lengths.

marks.description: The most boats marked at once.

wedges.description: Dirty air is drawn behind boats within this, in m.

wedgeDeficit.description: Out to where the wind's loss falls under this share.

Sky.title: Sky
Sky.description: The sky's numbers: the lengths of its day, year and month, its scale, the moment it is counted from, and the stars with names. Where each body stands follows from these and the time alone.

day.description: The day, sunrise to sunrise, in minutes.

year.description: The year, in days: the stars gain one turn on the sun in it.

month.description: The moon's month, new moon to new moon, in days.

scale.description: Degrees of the sky to a nautical mile on the water: a boat that many miles nearer a star's point sees it one degree higher.

epoch.description: Sky time zero, in seconds of UTC since 1970: the same in every world.

sunAtEpoch.description: The sun's angle past noon at the centre of the disk, at the epoch, in degrees.

starsAtEpoch.description: The stars' turn beyond the sun's at the epoch, in degrees.

moonAtEpoch.description: The moon's age at the epoch, in degrees past new.

stars.description: The stars with names, the brightest of the navigator's.

NamedStar.title: NamedStar
NamedStar.description: A star with a name, at its place in the Bright Star Catalogue (J2000).

number.description: Its number in the Bright Star Catalogue (HR).

declination.description: Declination, in degrees. 90 is the pole itself, which the stars turn about.

Light.title: Light
Light.description: A navigation light a boat shows from sunset to sunrise, by the arc it shows over (International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, Rule 21): a red sidelight to port and a green to starboard, each from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam; a white sternlight over the 135° astern; or the three combined in one lantern at the masthead, which Rule 25(b) allows a sailing vessel of less than 20 m.

Id.description: Stable identifier of a kind, stored in the database: never renamed or reused.

ArtPath.description: Path of an art file, relative to the repository's art/ folder.

BoatArt.title: BoatArt
BoatArt.description: A boat's art. Every art object's values are paths under art/, checked to exist.

model.description: The boat's model: a glTF binary with the nodes hull, mast, boom, sail, telltales, pennant, rudder, tiller, daggerboard and sailor, and a node for each of the boat's lights, named as the light, where its lantern is.

far.description: The boat's far model, drawn for boats seen from afar among many: the model's nodes but telltales, pennant and lights, with few segments.

model.description: The sailor's model: a glTF binary with the nodes body, head, arm-left and arm-right, its origin at the hips, facing +x.

far.description: The sailor's far model, drawn in boats seen from afar: the model's nodes, with few segments.

Machine.title: Machine
Machine.description: The look of the machine sailors AI accounts sail as: the choices a player makes one from, a version, a metal finish and a main colour. A machine sailor's sailor keeps the three ids.

finishes.description: The finishes of its metal, each with its colour.

colours.description: Its main colours, chosen to stay apart for colour-blind players.

name.description: Display name, as the player reads it: lowercase but where a name is a proper noun.

colour.description: Its colour, sRGB, #rrggbb; none for a version.

description.description: What the boat is, in a few words.

capacity.description: Most people aboard, the skipper included.

beam.description: Greatest width of the hull, in metres.

lights.description: The navigation lights the boat shows by night. Together their arcs make the full circle once.

lookout.description: How high its lookout's eye is above the sea, in m: what it sees over the horizon.

BoatPhysics.title: BoatPhysics
BoatPhysics.description: The boat's physics, in SI units with angles in degrees. Every value is required.

PhysicsHull.title: PhysicsHull
PhysicsHull.description: The hull: its mass, resistance, inertia and stability.

displacement.description: Boat, rig and sailor, in kg.

waterlineLength.description: Length on the waterline, in m.

hullDraught.description: The hull's own draught, foils aside, in m.

centreOfGravity.description: Height of the centre of gravity above the waterline, in m.

dragAreaStep.description: Speed between entries of dragArea, in m/s.

dragArea.description: Upright resistance as a drag area (C_D A), at speeds 0, 1, 2 … times dragAreaStep, in m². Beyond the last, the last.
